before.question: I survived abuse in the troubled teen industry — do I have legal options?
before.answer: If you or a loved one survived abuse at a therapeutic boarding school, residential treatment center, wilderness program, boot camp or behavior modification facility, you may have legal options. It may be possible to seek compensation against the institutions and individuals who caused the harm. These cases are sensitive and complex, and Roden Law offers a completely free and confidential consultation to discuss your situation with a compassionate attorney.

before.question: What compensation could survivors of troubled teen industry abuse recover?
before.answer: Survivors may be eligible to recover compensation for the physical, emotional and psychological harm they endured, including long-term effects such as PTSD, depression, anxiety and related conditions. Every survivor's experience is different, and the damages available depend on the specific circumstances. Our attorneys will listen with care and help you understand what pursuing a claim could involve.

before.question: Is my consultation confidential, and what does it cost?
before.answer: Your consultation is completely free and completely confidential, and it does not need to be in person. There is no obligation to move forward. If we represent you and you have a case, there are no upfront costs or fees — we only get paid if you do. You can call 1-844-RESULTS 24/7 to speak with an experienced, compassionate attorney.

before.question: What kinds of abuse do these lawsuits involve?
before.answer: Allegations against these institutions have included physical abuse, psychological torment and humiliation, isolation, chemical restraints, neglect, deceptive marketing and other serious mistreatment. Many facilities have faced scrutiny for a lack of regulation, transparency and oversight. If you endured this type of abuse at a reform school, boarding school or similar institution, our attorneys are prepared to handle your case with the care and tenacity it deserves.

before.question: I was abused years ago — is it too late to file?
before.answer: It may not be too late. Statute-of-limitations rules for abuse survivors often extend the window to come forward, and these rules vary by state and circumstances. Because timelines can be complicated, we encourage you to reach out for a confidential consultation rather than assuming your time has passed. An attorney can review your situation and explain the options that may still be available to you.

before.question: Can Georgia and South Carolina survivors bring a claim with Roden Law?
before.answer: Yes. Roden Law is licensed in Georgia and South Carolina and has decades of experience advocating for injured and abused victims. Claims may proceed against the facilities and operators responsible for the abuse. We handle every case with sensitivity and confidentiality, and there are no upfront fees. Call 1-844-RESULTS anytime to talk through your situation.
